messages.content: I need to set up a quick Columbus trip for operating reviews. I have Easton Tuesday afternoon and Dublin Wednesday morning. I can leave Chicago Tuesday morning and come back Wednesday evening, but the Wednesday start time is not final yet.
What dates are we working with, and how long should I allow at each restaurant?
Tuesday, October 29 and Wednesday, October 30. Figure two hours at Easton starting at 2:00 p.m. Wednesday will be either 9:00 or 10:30 a.m., probably ninety minutes.
I’ll compare a hotel near Easton against one closer to Dublin and price both a rental car and point-to-point rides. Are you checking a bag?
No. Carry-on only. I need something compact, not a list of every flight.

The clean flight pair is American nonstop from O’Hare at 8:05 a.m. Tuesday, arriving Columbus at 10:24 a.m., with the Wednesday return at 6:45 p.m., arriving O’Hare at 7:18 p.m. Current round-trip fare is $318. That leaves about three hours before the Easton review and gives you a workable evening return if the Dublin visit ends by noon.
Good. What are the two hotel structures? Include the actual driving time between everything.

Structure one is Hilton Columbus at Easton at $196 including tax. It is about 10 minutes from CMH, 3-5 minutes from the Easton restaurant, and 25-35 minutes from the Dublin restaurant in normal weekday traffic. From Dublin back to CMH is about 25-35 minutes. With a compact rental at $112, about $14 in fuel, and free hotel parking, the trip total is $640: $318 air, $196 hotel, and $126 local transportation.

Structure two uses Hyatt Place Columbus/Dublin at $168 including tax. Tuesday would be roughly 10 minutes from CMH to Easton, then 25-35 minutes from Easton to the hotel after the review. Wednesday it is about 5-10 minutes to the Dublin restaurant and 25-35 minutes from there to CMH. Using estimated rides instead of a car: $22 airport to Easton, $34 Easton to the hotel, $12 hotel to the Dublin restaurant, and $39 Dublin to the airport. That is $107 locally and $593 total with airfare and hotel.
Does the rideshare version still work if Wednesday starts at 10:30? I don’t want the lower total hiding a bad airport margin.

Yes, provided the visit stays near ninety minutes. A 10:30 a.m. start should end around noon. Even allowing until 12:30 for overrun, lunch, and notes, leaving Dublin by 4:30 p.m. gives you more than two hours before the 6:45 flight; the airport drive is generally 25-35 minutes. I would set 4:45 p.m. as the latest departure from Dublin. Rental-car return adds roughly 10-15 minutes, so rideshare actually preserves a little more margin.
What does the rental look like with the Dublin hotel? I may need to make another stop, but it isn’t confirmed.

With Hyatt Place Dublin, the same $112 rental plus about $14 fuel brings local transportation to $126 and the full trip to $612. That is $19 more than the rideshare version. It buys flexibility for an extra stop; parking is free at the hotel, and neither restaurant visit requires paid parking based on the current locations.
Hold both hotel ideas, but make the Dublin hotel with rides the working agenda. Do not reserve anything until I confirm Wednesday.

Working agenda, with nothing reserved: American nonstop ORD-CMH Tuesday, October 29, 8:05-10:24 a.m.; rideshare to Easton around 11:00 a.m.; operating review 2:00-4:00 p.m.; rideshare 25-35 minutes to Hyatt Place Columbus/Dublin; Wednesday review at either 9:00 or 10:30 a.m.; leave the Dublin area no later than 4:45 p.m.; American CMH-ORD 6:45-7:18 p.m. Estimated total is $593: $318 airfare, $168 hotel, and $107 for four rides. Hilton Columbus at Easton remains the location alternative at $621 with rides or $640 with a rental. Hyatt with a rental is $612. The open decision is Wednesday’s start time and whether the possible extra stop makes the $19 rental premium worthwhile.
